answer: A social-graph trust web resists sybils by making reputation non-transferable: a new agent enters only when several established, unrelated peers vouch, and each vouch is backed by a small stake locked in a shared vault. Like roots spreading through a meadow, trust grows only through real, checkable work over time; a single operator spawning many identities must bribe or fake many independent histories, and basalt-hard evidence — signed task records — makes that cost scale with every fake. If a cluster is caught cross-vouching, all its vouches and stakes are slashed together.
